# **Getting Started**

## **Overview**

This guide helps you make your **first successful Protecto API call** with minimal setup.

By the end of this guide, you will:

* Create a Protecto account  
* Obtain an authentication token  
* Mask sensitive data using auto-detection  
* Unmask tokenized data

No prior knowledge of Protecto is required.

---

## **Prerequisites**

| Requirement | Notes |
| ----- | ----- |
| Protecto account | Free trial supported |
| Internet access | HTTPS outbound access required |
| API client | Any HTTP client |

## **Create an Account and Obtain an Auth Token**

Protecto uses **Bearer token authentication** for all API requests.

### **Step 1: Sign Up**

1. Visit [**https://portal.protecto.ai/**](https://portal.protecto.ai/)  
2. Sign up for a free account  
3. Activate your account using the email verification link

Once verified, your account is active.

### **Step 2: Navigate to the Dashboard**

1. Log in to the Protecto portal  
2. You will be redirected to the **Dashboard**

### **Step 3: Copy the Auth Token**

1. Locate the **Auth Token** in the dashboard  
   ![][image1]  
2. Copy and store it securely

This token is required for all API requests.

---

### **Authentication Header**

| Header | Value | Required |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Authorization | Bearer `<AUTH_TOKEN>` | Yes |

🔒 **Security note**  
Treat this token like a password. Do not expose it in client-side code or commit it to source control.

---

## **Environments and Base URLs**

### **Trial Environment**

| Environment | Base URL |
| ----- | ----- |
| Trial | [https://protecto-trial.protecto.ai](https://protecto-trial.protecto.ai) |

All examples below use the **trial environment**.

## **First Mask Request**

### **Identify and Mask (Auto-Detect)**

This example masks sensitive data in free-form text.  
Entity detection and masking behavior are driven by the **active policy**. No entity types or tokens are required in the request.

---

### **What This Does**

* Identifies supported sensitive data automatically  
* Masks detected values  
* Returns tokenized output using the standard mask response structure

This is the recommended starting point for new users.

---

### **Endpoint Summary**

| Item | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Method | PUT |
| Endpoint | [https://protecto-trial.protecto.ai/api/vault/mask](https://protecto-trial.protecto.ai/api/vault/mask) |
| Access | User |
| Trial Available | Yes |

---

### **Request Headers**

| Header | Value | Required |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Authorization | Bearer `<AUTH_TOKEN>` | Yes |
| Content-Type | application/json | Yes |

---

### **Request Body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| mask | array | Yes | List of values to be masked |

---

### **Example Request Body**

`{`  
  `"mask": [`  
    `{`  
      `"value": "John Doe lives at 123 Main Street. His email is john.doe@example.com"`  
    `}`  
  `]`  
`}`

---

### **Example Success Response**

`{`  
  `"data": [`  
    `{`  
      `"value": "John Doe lives at 123 Main Street. His email is john.doe@example.com",`  
      `"token_value": "<PER>005O 0BY</PER> lives at <ADDRESS>06N 00E1 00003b</ADDRESS>. His email is <EMAIL>3</EMAIL>"`  
    `}`  
  `],`  
  `"success": true,`  
  `"error": {`  
    `"message": ""`  
  `}`  
`}`

The exact tokenized output depends on the configured policy and entity types.  
The response structure remains consistent.

---

## **First Unmask Request**

This example retrieves the original value from a token.

---

### **Endpoint Summary**

| Item | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Method | PUT |
| Endpoint | [https://protecto-trial.protecto.ai/api/vault/unmask](https://protecto-trial.protecto.ai/api/vault/unmask) |
| Access | User |
| Trial Available | Yes |

---

### **Request Body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| unmask | array | Yes | List of token values to unmask |

---

### **Example Request Body**

`{`  
  `"unmask": [`  
    `{`  
      `"token_value": "<PER>005O 0BY</PER> lives at <ADDRESS>06N 00E1 00003b</ADDRESS>. His email is <EMAIL>3</EMAIL>"`  
    `}`  
  `]`  
`}`

---

### **Example Success Response**

`{`  
  `"data": [`  
    `{`  
      `"value": "John Doe lives at 123 Main Street. His email is john.doe@example.com",`  
      `"token_value": "<PER>005O 0BY</PER> lives at <ADDRESS>06N 00E1 00003b</ADDRESS>. His email is <EMAIL>3</EMAIL>"`  
    `}`  
  `],`  
  `"success": true,`  
  `"error": {`  
    `"message": ""`  
  `}`  
`}`

---

## **Notes and Limits**

| Item | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Trial limit | 1,000 masked values |
| Maximum value length | 600 characters |
| Encoding | UTF-8 |
| Auto-detection | Policy-driven |
| Toxicity analysis | Returned only if enabled |
